chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Fletcher Henderson, Kirby and swinging softly
summary: Fletcher's classical touches led Kirby to feature small-band softness; Ramirez illustrates with the hearing range and a tiny calling card.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Exactly. Look at Fletcher, his orchestra... Fletcher used to have an arrangement on waltzes, elegy, and he used to play the Classics and everything else. Later John Kirby came from that band, and he really featured playing the Classics, and playing the small band, and playing softly -- because he believed you could swing just as effective softly as you can loud!
Well, I think that's true enough. Don't you?
Oh yes. In those days... If you speak to me in a modulated tone of voice and it's out of range, I'll have to say "What did you say?" Then you repeat it. Then I'm within your hearing range. Right?

Exactly. As far as a parallel to that, I'll illustrate that as far as the eyes can see. A girl gave me a card, a calling card, and the lettering on this was so small, I had to take a magnifying glass... I said, "Why did you do this?" She says, "But by the time...the trouble you have to see my name, you'll remember... You'll know who I am." [LAUGHS] It made sense.
